jobs.title: Principal Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Principal Embedded Software Engineer to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Embedded Software & FPGA Manager, the Principal Embedded Software Engineer will lead the architecture, development, and integration of embedded software across multiple satellite programs, ensuring robust, reliable, and high‑performance mission solutions. Key Duties and Responsibilities Develop and maintain embedded software and support hardware bring‑up on satellite modules. Architect, design, develop, and maintain embedded software (Linux, RTOS, bare metal) for satellite systems. Collaborate with cross‑functional engineering teams to define and refine software requirements. Serve as the technical lead for multiple satellite programs. Create and maintain unit tests using Test‑Driven Development methodologies. Develop and automate system‑level tests. Build software for specialized payloads, including imagers, image processors, communication devices, and astronomical science instruments. Integrate and test software in simulation, flight‑replica, flight‑vehicle, and hardware‑in‑the‑loop environments. Lead and mentor junior software engineers, providing technical guidance and task direction. Represent Terran Orbital in technical working groups and customer interactions. Support the security of embedded systems. Support occasional travel (up to 10%) to customer or vendor sites for design reviews and collaborative technical work. Required Qualifications and Skil

jobs.title: Sr. Manufacturing Engineer - EPS
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Sr. Manufacturing Engineer to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Integrated Product Team (IPT) Lead – Electrical Power Systems (EPS), the Sr. Manufacturing Engineer will develop and implement optimal, cost-effective manufacturing processes and methods in accordance with product specifications and quality standards. This role will be supporting manufacturing issues on existing product designs and new satellite mechanisms early in the design phase, providing critical design for manufacturability input and supporting testing of these assemblies, while developing and implementing the plan to move from design/test into build/production. Specifically, this position will focus on the Electrical Power System (EPS) component and module team, ensuring that all processes and methods are tailored to the unique requirements of EPS components and modules, enhancing their reliability and performance in satellite applications. Key Duties and Responsibilities Execute, maintain, and evolve the company manufacturing strategy and technology roadmap in line with Terran Orbital strategy. Design and implement the production floor layout, as it relates to manufacturing flight hardware. Design for modularity and adaptability, with an eye for scaling with time and product evolution. jobs.title: Staff FPGA Design Engineer
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Staff FPGA Design Engineer to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Embedded Software & FPGA Manager, the Staff FPGA Design Engineer will lead the architecture, development, verification, and flight-readiness of FPGA-based avionics subsystems. This role owns FPGA RTL design from concept through qualification, integration, and mission operations. The engineer collaborates across avionics, embedded software, systems, and hardware teams to deliver high-reliability, flight-critical digital logic. Key Duties and Responsibilities Own FPGA RTL development from architecture definition through verification, integration and flight readiness. Define FPGA architecture and requirements in collaboration with systems, hardware and embedded software teams. Develop RTL in SystemVerilog or VHDL for Microship Polarfire and AMD Zynq US+ and Versal. Perform comprehensive verification, including simulation, test benches, timing closure, resource analysis and hardware validation. Lead design reviews, ensure requirement traceability, and produce documentation for FPGA operation and integration. Define and execute verification and validation testing (DVT) and support board bring-up. Support system bring-up, integration, and troubleshooting during avionics and flight test activities. Lead cross-functional technical discussions, drive architecture decisions and mentor more junior engineers. Required Qualifications and Skills Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Eng

jobs.title: Systems Integration Engineer II/III (Weekend Shift)
jobs.description_text: Terran Orbital is seeking an experienced Systems Integration Engineer to join our dynamic team. Reporting to the Manager, Systems Integration & Test the Systems Integration Engineer will work within a multidisciplinary team to build, integrate, and test space vehicles at both the sub-system and system levels. This role is on our Weekend Shift (Friday-Sunday) from 6:00AM – 7:00PM. We are open to a level II (Engineer) or level III (Sr. Engineer) for this position. Key Duties and Responsibilities Design assembly and testing campaigns. Write, review, and execute assembly and test procedures. Manage work orders and drive nonconformances. Resolve electrical and mechanical issues, debugging at the satellite system and sub-system level. Responsible for enabling day-to-day execution of the vehicle integration and test flow. Evaluate proposed designs for manufacturability and integration. Interface with engineers and technicians to advance to larger-scale manufacturing and automation. Design and develop tools and hardware to enable vehicle assembly and ensure vehicle testing abilities. The position will require being hands-on and will require standing for extended periods. Able to work on multiple highly complex major projects requiring innovative, original solutions. Plans multiple projects simultaneously. jobs.description_text: Tecovas is looking for a conceptually strong, collaborative Art Director to help shape how our brand shows up in the world. Lead the visual direction of integrated campaigns, seasonal collections, product launches, and collaborations from concept through final delivery. Partner with copywriters to develop ideas in which visual and verbal storytelling work together, and present concepts and the reasoning behind them to creative and marketing leadership. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more. Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. jobs.title: Lead, Test & Launch Operations Engineer - Launch Pad
jobs.description_text: NEUTRON Neutron is a medium-lift launch vehicle being developed by Rocket Lab, a publicly traded end-to-end space company. The rocket can deliver the mega constellations of tomorrow, enable interplanetary payloads, and support human spaceflight. As a reusable platform, Neutron will deliver a very cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab's proven history with Electron – the second most launched rocket, worldwide, in 2024. If you're interested in joining an incredible team in a fast-paced and rewarding environment, this is your opportunity. HASTE HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron) is a specialized variant of Rocket Lab's proven Electron launch vehicle, designed to support hypersonic flight testing and research missions. Operating from Rocket Lab's Launch Complex 2 at Wallops Island, Virginia, Electron HASTE provides a unique capability to deliver hypersonic test vehicles to the required flight conditions for cutting-edge aerodynamic and propulsion research. The program represents an exciting evolution of the Electron platform, supporting critical national defense and aerospace research objectives while maintaining Rocket Lab's commitment to rapid, reliable launch operations. Our Space Systems team builds everything from complete spacecraft, precision payloads to the components and subsystems that allow them to thrive in space, like solar panels, flight software, star trackers, optical systems, separation systems, radios, and more. Our Space Systems team has enabled more than 1,700 missions, ranging from interplanetary exploration, in-space manufacturing to national security and defense initiatives. The team has built spacecraft, payloads, and components for missions to the Moon and Mars, working with partners including NASA, the Space Development Agency, and the U.S. Space Force. Whether it’s a single high-performance spacecraft, constellation, or the vertically integrated components that help them get to space — our world class Space Systems team is empowering some of the boldest and most ambitious space missions. SENIOR SYSTEMS SAFETY ENGINEER I Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. At Rocket Lab, our Safety & Mission Assurance Team is at the heart of every successful launch. As a Senior Systems Safety Engineer I, you’ll play a critical role in working with range safety authorities to ensure the safe ground processing of spacecraft and ground support equipment at launch ranges.
